issues.body: The new rationale says ignoring `unlabeled` leaves the wider scope decision standing until the next push. However, this workflow remains subscribed to every `labeled` event and has no job-level label guard. After `ci-full` is removed, adding any unrelated label starts both jobs and evaluates the current label set without `ci-full`, so the scope can narrow before a push. The same overstatement is repeated in the wiring test and documentation; the test verifies only trigger membership, not persistence of the previously wider decision.
issues.fix_hint: Change the claims to say the wider result stands only until the next subscribed event (including any later `labeled` event) or push. Explicitly distinguish the four guarded ci-select callers from unguarded `vectorized-feature-off.yml`, and adjust the focused test's docstring/messages so they do not claim an invariant the test cannot prove.
issues.title: Wider scope does not necessarily stand until the next push

verdict.summary: The trigger reduction itself is plausible, but the central documented and tested guarantee is overstated. Removing a *-full label does not necessarily leave the wider selection standing until the next push: any later `labeled` event retriggers these workflows, and `vectorized-feature-off.yml` explicitly has no label-event guard, so an unrelated label addition reruns its scope decision with `ci-full` absent. The focused test only checks the static event-type lists and cannot establish the claimed persistence behavior. Revise the rationale and test commentary to state the actual boundary (next subscribed `labeled` event or push), especially for the unguarded vectorized workflow.
